actions.action: Freeze session membership at a committed watermark.
actions.mechanism: Promise exactly IDs created by watermark W and not deleted by W; payloads remain current, not historical.
actions.implementation: Persist birth and deletion versions; publish W only after all changes through W are visible. Restrict membership filters to immutable fields.
actions.check: Capture expected membership at W. Later inserts must be absent; later deletions must remain represented by their IDs.
actions.risk: Per-record versions alone cannot establish a global committed watermark.

actions.action: Replace offsets with a stable seek cursor.
actions.mechanism: An exclusive creation-timestamp-and-ID boundary prevents position shifts; immutable IDs break timestamp ties.
actions.implementation: Index the ordering pair. Query membership at W strictly after the cursor pair, ordered ascending; advance using the last returned entry.
actions.check: Insert and delete around page boundaries, including equal timestamps. Concatenated pages must equal the expected ordered IDs without duplicates.
actions.risk: Mutable sorting fields invalidate this ordering guarantee.

actions.action: Return deleted IDs as explicit browse entries.
actions.mechanism: Tombstone entries preserve frozen membership even when record bodies disappear between requests.
actions.implementation: Retain ID, ordering fields, birth version, deletion version, and immutable filter fields for 24 hours. Deleted entries consume page slots.
actions.check: Delete unread members after page one. Their IDs must appear once as deleted entries; pre-watermark deletions must never appear.
actions.risk: Clients must handle deleted entries rather than silently discarding them.

actions.action: Expire cursors before required tombstones disappear.
actions.mechanism: Bounded session lifetimes make the membership promise compatible with finite deletion retention.
actions.implementation: Set a fixed ten-minute expiry at session creation. Sign W, boundary, filters, ordering, and expiry; reject expired cursors without silently restarting.
actions.check: A six-page, two-minute browse succeeds. Expired and modified cursors fail explicitly, including when deleted records have been purged.
actions.risk: Longer browsing requires an explicit restart, not seamless continuation.

actions.action: Consider an existing-store ID manifest instead.
actions.mechanism: Alternative: an immutable ordered ID list freezes membership without repeated historical membership queries.
actions.implementation: Within one request-scoped consistent read, persist ordered IDs in the existing store. Page by manifest position; expire after ten minutes.
actions.check: Enable only if capture, persistence, and response meet 300 ms under load. Concurrent mutations must not alter manifest IDs.
actions.risk: Capturing 80,000 IDs may exceed latency or storage budgets.

actions.action: Make duplicate and omission checks an executable oracle.
actions.mechanism: A reference membership set distinguishes correct browsing from merely duplicate-free output.
actions.implementation: Run randomized insert/delete schedules against captured membership. Compare six-page output with its expected prefix; also drain complete sessions against the full sequence.
actions.check: Assert ordered equality, unique ID count, and empty expected-minus-observed and observed-minus-expected sets for completed traversals.
actions.risk: Checking uniqueness alone misses omissions; partial sessions need prefix expectations.

actions.action: Gate deployment on worst-case indexed query behavior.
actions.mechanism: Seek pagination can still scan many excluded inserts or tombstones; an index alone does not establish latency.
actions.implementation: Inspect query plans and load-test 80,000 records with concurrent writes and retained tombstones. Add covering indexes for ordering and membership metadata.
actions.check: Measure end-to-end requests, including session creation and late pages; reject designs producing responses above 300 ms in the defined workload.
actions.risk: Benchmarks cannot guarantee latency under unspecified load; define supported concurrency.
